description: This is a false-colour satellite image acquired by Spot 5 on 2011-08-01, showing the marshes and estuary of the Guadalquivir river within the Doñana Natura 2000 site in Spain. The image, with a spatial resolution of 2.5 metres, uses a 1/2/3 band combination where healthy vegetation appears in bright red hues. On the right, a dark blue area represents a large body of water, indicating the coastline. Inland, the landscape is characterised by irregular dark channels and water bodies, typical of an estuarine system. Numerous distinct, geometrically rectangular areas of vibrant red are visible, strongly suggesting agricultural fields (such as rice fields, consistent with the document's context of "salt marshes transformed to agriculture"). These cultivated areas are interspersed with patches of lighter red, pink, and grey tones, which likely represent less vegetated marshlands, mudflats, or moist soil.
